description: Search across curated tools, MCP servers, prompts, skills, and trending repos, one query, every corner of the ecosystem.

summary.one_liner: A large, community-maintained, categorized directory of AI tools and resources, with each entry annotated by pricing tags (free, freemium, paid, opensource).
summary.what_it_does: This is a curated "awesome"-style list of AI tools, organized into about 70 category sections such as Art, Chatbots, Developer Tools, Data & BI, Audio & Speech, and Design. Each entry is a one-line bullet with the tool name, a short description, and hashtag pricing tags like #free, #freemium, #paid, or #opensource. Some sections also tag entries with #mcp, #api, or #rag. The README describes the list as a community collection that accepts pull requests to add services, and it points to a separate contribution guide. The README excerpt shown is truncated, so the full set of categories and entries is not visible here. The repository metadata describes a search site that covers tools, MCP servers, prompts, skills, and trending repos. The README itself does not document how that search works, so this summary does not describe it.
use_cases: Finding an AI tool for a specific task such as image generation or transcription
Comparing free versus paid AI services in a category
Discovering AI coding assistants and agent tools
Browsing MCP-enabled services for AI assistants
Contributing new AI tool listings via pull request
notable: Pricing hashtags (#free, #freemium, #paid, #opensource) on each entry for filtering
Broad category coverage from 3D and Agriculture to Developer Tools and Crypto
Open to community pull requests with contribution guidelines
Entries include MCP-server and API-tagged tools useful for AI agent builders
caveats: The README is truncated, so the full list is not visible to this summary
Many listings are promotional, and entries are not verified by this summary
Some entries are marketing copy rather than neutral descriptions
